skill.name: literature-review
skill.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews across scientific databases, verify citations, synthesize evidence, and generate polished review documents.
skill.summary: Plan, search, synthesize, verify, and format academic literature reviews.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, reference links, and ordinary literature-review terminology. Confirmed risks are limited to intended outbound citation verification, local output file writes, and Pandoc PDF generation on user-supplied documents.

remediation.issue: Pandoc is invoked on user-supplied markdown files.
remediation.suggestion: Run PDF generation only on trusted local documents, keep shell execution disabled, and document that Pandoc may read included resources during conversion.

remediation.issue: Output paths can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict generated reports to a dedicated output directory or warn users before writing outside the working directory.

remediation.issue: Citation verification sends extracted DOI values to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the DOI and CrossRef requests and allow users to skip verification for sensitive or unpublished drafts.

remediation.issue: The skill documentation includes package installation and command examples.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review local dependency installation commands before running them, especially on shared or managed systems.

content.value_statement: Literature reviews require careful search design, citation checks, and transparent synthesis. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured review workflow with reusable templates and scripts.
actual_capabilities: Defines research questions, scope, inclusion criteria, and database search strategy.
Guides searches across PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, Semantic Scholar, and specialized scientific databases.
Deduplicates, ranks, filters, and formats exported search results from JSON input.
Verifies DOI resolution and retrieves citation metadata from DOI and CrossRef services.
Provides templates for thematic synthesis, PRISMA-style documentation, and quality assessment.
Generates markdown and Pandoc-based PDF review outputs when dependencies are installed.
limitations: It does not guarantee access to subscription-only papers or restricted databases.
Citation verification depends on external DOI and CrossRef service availability.
PDF generation requires local Pandoc and LaTeX tools installed by the user.
Search results still require human screening and subject-matter judgment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a biomedical systematic review
use_cases.description: Plan a PICO question, search multiple biomedical sources, screen results, and document methods for reproducibility.

use_cases.title: Draft a thesis literature chapter
use_cases.description: Organize prior work by themes, identify gaps, and create consistent citations for a graduate research chapter.

use_cases.title: Map a technical research area
use_cases.description: Combine preprints, journal articles, and citation chaining to summarize the state of the art.

prompt_templates.title: Start a focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a literature review on [topic]. Define the research question, scope, inclusion criteria, and three databases to search.

prompt_templates.title: Build a search strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create database-specific search strings for [research question]. Include synonyms, Boolean logic, date limits, and documentation fields.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize selected papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize these selected papers by theme, compare methods and findings, assess evidence quality, and identify research gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Finalize a publication-ready review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my draft literature review for search reproducibility, thematic synthesis, citation accuracy, limitations, and final PDF readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan a review on CRISPR therapies for sickle cell disease.
output: A focused PICO research question with population, intervention, comparison, and outcomes.
A database plan covering PubMed, bioRxiv, Semantic Scholar, and clinical trial sources.
A screening and quality assessment checklist aligned with systematic review practice.

output_examples.input: Summarize these search results by theme.
output: Thematic sections that compare delivery methods, efficacy evidence, safety concerns, and evidence gaps.
A concise limitations section that distinguishes study limitations from review limitations.
A list of priority questions for future research.

output_examples.input: Prepare the review for final submission.
output: A citation verification report with failed DOI checks highlighted for correction.
A final quality checklist covering search documentation, references, figures, and PDF formatting.

best_practices: Define the research question, scope, and inclusion criteria before searching.
Search at least three complementary databases and record each search string and date.
Verify citations and review generated documents before relying on the final output.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one database for a comprehensive review.
Do not treat preprints and peer-reviewed papers as equal evidence without noting status.
Do not accept generated citations without DOI and metadata verification.

faq.question: Can this skill perform a full systematic review automatically?
faq.answer: It can structure and accelerate the workflow, but human screening and expert judgment remain required.

faq.question: Which databases does it support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for PubMed, PubMed Central, arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Semantic Scholar, and specialized biomedical sources.

faq.question: Does it verify citations?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled verifier extracts DOIs, checks DOI resolution, and retrieves CrossRef metadata when available.

faq.question: Can it generate PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, when Pandoc and a LaTeX engine such as xelatex are installed locally.

faq.question: Does it support citation styles?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for APA, Nature, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE style conventions.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-biomedical topics?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow also supports technical and scientific reviews that use arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and related sources.
